# 4c Fetch URLs, Phase 4 exit: contract

**Read first:** [build README → Phase 4](./README.md#phase-4-router-scripts) (and its Phase 1–3 sections), [script generation](../processes/router-scripts/script-generation.md) ("Steps — getting it onto the router", Rules, the edge cases about fetch URLs and downloads), [router scripts module](../modules/router-scripts.md) (Generations), [architecture → HTTP surfaces](../architecture.md#http-surfaces) (public routes), [router sync](../processes/routing/router-sync.md) step 5 (awaiting setup, the probe), design `RP-Script-generation`, and the **As built** of 4a, 4b, 2b (the public `/s/{token}`, `web.Limiter`, `httpx.MaskPath`), 3d (the public `/r/…` and its tests) and 3f (the probe, `routingtest.Registered`).

**Done when:** a generation gets a fetch URL that works once and for 1 hour, and a new one ends the old; the generation page shows it masked with **Reveal** and **Copy** beside the two RouterOS commands; `GET /f/{token}` answers the filled file once, records `routerscript.fetched` (which notifies) and answers `404` afterwards; an unused URL answers `404` after its hour and the scan records `routerscript.fetch_url_expired`; the generation page follows the router after the import (fetched, Proxier's key, connected and synced) and lists every fetch URL; the end-to-end test goes from publishing to the router's first sync; the exit demo is written for the user; every checklist line has its test.

## Decisions

| Topic | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Create | `POST /router-scripts/generations/:id/fetch-url`: **Create fetch URL** (primary), or **New fetch URL…** while one waits (strength 1: "A new URL makes this one stop working."). One `Write`: a waiting URL of the generation ends first, as `replaced` when it was still valid or as `expired` (with its `routerscript.fetch_url_expired`) when its hour had passed and the scan hadn't seen it yet; then the new row with `vault.NewToken()` sealed as `fetch_url:<id>:token` (inserted as `X''` with its lookup, sealed with the new id in the same transaction), `expires_at = now + 1 h`, `created_by`; `routerscript.fetch_url_created{expires, replaced}`. A generation of an archived script can still get one (it is the generation that is fetched); the URL-changed band (4b) stays above it. | script-generation.md "Create fetch URL"; "Creating a fetch URL invalidates any earlier unused fetch URL". |
| URL and commands | The URL is `<PROXIER_BASE_URL>/f/<token>`; the commands are `/tool fetch url="<url>" dst-path=<slug>.rsc` and `/import <slug>.rsc`, built by `generations.Commands` (the only place they are written). | script-generation.md step 2. |
| Fetch URL area | On the generation page (RP-Script-generation's "Fetch URL · works once"): the URL masked (`https://proxier.tikhonnnnn.com/f/••••••••`) with **Reveal** / **Hide** (`GET …/fetch-url/reveal`, a `no-store` fragment with the real URL and commands) and **Copy** (`data-copy` carrying the real URL: one tap, as links' Copy URL; the page is `no-store`); its state line `#fetch-url-state` ("expires at 17:30 · in 58 min", later "used at 16:41", "expired · create a new one"); the note "Paste into the new router's terminal after the prerequisites in the script's header. The router needs the internet to fetch: after a reset with no-defaults, give its WAN port a DHCP client first."; the two commands, each with **Copy**, and **Copy both lines** (`y`); **New fetch URL…**. Without a waiting URL: "No fetch URL. One works once, for 1 hour." and **Create fetch URL**. No seconds countdown (the build README's rule). | `RP-Script-generation`; the first-fetch question is open question "to verify" 9. |
| Public fetch | `GET /f/:token` on `r.Public` (no cookies, `no-store`, `noindex`, 60 requests a minute per IP and `/f/•••` in Proxier's logs: already the platform's). Any other method, HEAD included, answers the plain `404` and uses nothing, whatever the router does with it. A token not shaped `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$` → `404` without a lookup. A lookup that finds no `waiting` row whose `expires_at > now` → `404`. Then the body is made (`Body`: unseal, `params.Fill`); a failure is a `500` and uses nothing. Then one `Write`: `UPDATE … SET state = 'used', ended_at, ip, user_agent, token = NULL, token_lookup = NULL WHERE id = ? AND state = 'waiting' AND expires_at > now`; no row → `404` (another request won); one row → `routerscript.fetched{ip, user_agent}` (actor `system`) in the same transaction. The answer: `200`, `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<file name>"`, the file. The URL is used up when Proxier answers, so a download cut short needs a new URL. `ip` is `c.RealIP()` (the platform's extractor), `user_agent` at most 256 characters. | script-generation.md steps 3–4; architecture.md "public routes". |
| Expiry scan | Schedule `routerscripts.fetch_urls` (`Every: 5m`) enqueues the job of the same name (queue `maintenance`, 1 attempt, step `expire`, `Quiet`): every `waiting` URL with `expires_at ≤ now` becomes `expired` (`ended_at = now`, token and lookup erased) with `routerscript.fetch_url_expired{expired: <its expiry>}`, one `Write` for the batch; nothing found, nothing recorded. The fetch itself never waits for the scan: an expired URL answers `404` at once. | script-generation.md step 5. |
| Notification | `routerscript.fetched` notifies by default, 📥. The module is a `NotificationRenderer` for it (an empty user agent must read well): EN "{subject} was fetched from {ip}" / "{user_agent}. Its fetch URL is used up." (without a user agent: "Its fetch URL is used up."), RU "{subject}: файл скачан с {ip}" / "{user_agent}. Ссылка для скачивания больше не работает." (without: "Ссылка для скачивания больше не работает."). `{subject}` is "Dacha · fresh-router v4". | events.md "fresh-router v4 for 'Parents' was fetched from 198.51.100.4". |
| After the import | An area on the generation page (RP-Script-generation's "After the import"), three numbered steps. **1 The router fetches the file**: "waiting" with a live URL ("You get a Telegram message with the router's IP when it happens."), "fetched at 16:41 from 198.51.100.4 · Mikrotik/7.24.5 Fetch" (the latest used URL), "the fetch URL expired unused", or "no fetch URL yet: create one above, or download the file". **2 Proxier's key**: with a `@fill proxier-ssh-key` parameter "The script lets Proxier's user log in with Proxier's key (proxierKey)."; without one, and with a router, "Add Proxier's key to the router" with the router's `KeyCommands` and **Copy**; without a router "Not needed: the router isn't registered for routing." **3 Proxier connects and runs the first sync** (from `RouterRegistrar.Router`): awaiting before its deadline "awaiting setup · Proxier tries Dacha every 10 min until 16 Oct, through dacha-pi."; after it "never connected · open the router and run Test connection"; active "connected at 16:52 · synced at 16:53" (or "first sync queued", or "first sync failed: <error>"); paused, removing, "removed from Routing", or "not registered for routing". The area polls (`hx-trigger="every 10s"`) only while something waits (a live URL, or a router awaiting or not synced yet) and stops by itself; each answer also swaps `#fetch-url-state` out of band, so a revealed URL stays revealed. | `RP-Script-generation`; ui/README "Long work is visible". |
| Fetch history | Every fetch URL of the generation, newest first: created (time, by), expires, and its state with its time: waiting; used (from IP · user agent); expired unused; replaced by a newer one. Kept forever, like generations (a few rows per router). | RP-Script-generation's "Fetch history". |
| Page layout | Desktop: the bands, then Fetch URL and After the import on the left, Generation and Values on the right, Fetch history and Activity below. Under 760 px: Fetch URL and After the import first, buttons full width. | Phone use is reacting and copying. |
| Retention | Generations and fetch URLs are kept; no prune job (a token never outlives its hour). | `data-model.md` retention gains the line. |
| End to end | `TestRouterSetUpEndToEnd` (`rscriptstest.WithModules` with jobs, a `routerostest` router that accepts Proxier's key): publish `paramstest.Annotated()`; generate "Parents" with a new link in "Family" and a new router at the fake router's address; create a fetch URL; `GET /f/<token>` → the file with the link's URL in `subUrl`, `to_vpn_list`, `vpn-doh` and Proxier's key; a second `GET` → `404`; run `routing.probe_round` → the router is pinned and active, `routing.router_connected` is recorded and the initial sync installs Main's services on the fake router; the generation page's After the import shows the fetch and the sync. The roadmap's exit, short of a real router. | Roadmap Phase 4 exit. |

## Go signatures

### `routerscripts/generations` additions

```go
const FetchURLLifetime = time.Hour

// Job type and schedule.
const JobFetchURLs = "routerscripts.fetch_urls"

type FetchURL struct {
	ID        int64
	State     string // waiting, used, expired, replaced
	CreatedAt time.Time
	CreatedBy string
	ExpiresAt time.Time
	EndedAt   time.Time
	IP        string
	UserAgent string
}

type Deps struct {
	/* 4b */
	BaseURL *url.URL
}

// Commands are the two lines pasted into the router's terminal.
func Commands(fetchURL, slug string) (fetch, imp string)
func (s *Service) CreateFetchURL(ctx context.Context, generationID int64, actor string) (FetchURL, string, error) // the URL
// Live is the waiting URL with its URL; false when none waits (or its hour passed).
func (s *Service) Live(ctx context.Context, generationID int64) (FetchURL, string, bool, error)
func (s *Service) FetchURLs(ctx context.Context, generationID int64) ([]FetchURL, error)            // newest first
// Register adds GET /f/:token to the public group.
func (s *Service) Register(g *echo.Group)
// Expire is the scan's step: the waiting URLs past their hour become expired.
func (s *Service) Expire(ctx context.Context, actor string) (int, error) // actor: the scan's job:<id> (As built)
func (s *Service) JobTypes() []jobs.Type
func (s *Service) Schedules() []jobs.Schedule
```

## Routes

| Method, path | What |
|---|---|
| `POST /router-scripts/generations/:gid/fetch-url` | Create (or replace) the fetch URL → the generation page |
| `GET /router-scripts/generations/:gid/fetch-url/reveal` | The URL and commands unmasked (`no-store`; `hide=1` masks again) |
| `GET /router-scripts/generations/:gid/after` | The After the import area (htmx polling; `#fetch-url-state` out of band) |
| `GET /f/:token` | Public: the filled file, once |

## Events

Recorded in 4c: `routerscript.fetch_url_created`, `routerscript.fetched` (notifies), `routerscript.fetch_url_expired`.

## Phase 4 exit demo

The user's, on the real deployment, with a spare MikroTik on RouterOS 7.24.5+ (the roadmap's exit: "a factory-reset router fetches its generation with `/tool fetch`, imports it, appears in Routing, and is synced without any manual step except installing Proxier's key"; with zero-touch built there is no manual step at all):

1. In `~/projects/mikrotik/fresh-router.rsc`: add `# END PARAMETERS` after `dohForwarder`; `# @fill subscription-link` directly above `:local subUrl`, `# @fill routing-address-list` above `:local vpnList`, `# @fill routing-doh-forwarder` above `:local dohForwarder`; a parameter for Proxier's key and the lines that use it, guarded so that a file without a key still imports, for example:

   ```
   # Proxier's public key: the proxier user logs in with it
   # @fill proxier-ssh-key
   :local proxierKey ""
   ```

   and, in the body (under `# system`):

   ```
   :if ([:len $proxierKey] > 0) do={
       /user group add name=proxier policy=read,write,ftp,ssh
       /user add name=proxier group=proxier password=[:rndstr length=32 from="abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789"]
       /user ssh-keys add user=proxier key=$proxierKey
   }
   ```

   The user gets a password nobody knows (Winbox and the console would otherwise accept an empty one). To verify on the router (open questions "to verify" 5 and 9): `:rndstr` on 7.24.5, `/user ssh-keys add … key=` from an imported script, the group's policy for `/import` of the service blocks. If a DHCP client is added by hand for the fetch (step 4), the script's own `/ip dhcp-client add interface=$wanIface` may refuse a second client on the port: `:do { /ip dhcp-client remove [find interface=$wanIface] } on-error={}` before it avoids that. Update the header's USAGE and PREREQUISITES (no `mtvpn.py`, no manual key).
2. Deploy the image with Phase 4. Router scripts → **New script**: upload the file. The panel shows 19 parameters, `vpnGateway` computed, no problems. **Publish v1**.
3. **Generate for a new router**: router name ("Dacha"), **Register a new router** on "Main" with its LAN address (`<lanNet>.1`) and the jump host that reaches it (already confirmed in Proxier: the probe never pins a jump host), **Create a link** in a subscription. The summary lists the link, the router and the file; generate. Routing → Routers shows Dacha awaiting setup.
4. On the router: `/system reset-configuration no-defaults=yes skip-backup=yes keep-users=yes`, then the script's prerequisites (device mode with `fetch=yes`, the container package, the USB disk), a temporary DHCP client on the WAN port if there is no internet. **Create fetch URL**, paste both lines.
5. Telegram: "Dacha · fresh-router v1 was fetched from <IP>". Fetching the same URL again answers `404`.
6. Within 10 minutes the probe pins the router's key; Dacha is active, `router_connected` and the first sync follow; the generation page's After the import shows all three steps done. On the router `/ip dns static print where comment=<a tag of Main>` lists the domains; mihomo runs with `SUB1` = the link (its fetch appears on the link page).
7. Write into this contract's **As built**: `/tool fetch`'s user agent, what the key and user lines needed on 7.24.5, the DHCP-client question, timings, anything that differed.

## As built

Built 2026-10-09. Every checklist line but the exit demo has its test of that name in that file; `make check` (with `check-editor`), `make lint` (0 issues) and `docker build .` are green. Every package of the module still runs under `-race`, the end-to-end test included.

**Packages** as in Files: `generations/fetchurls.go` (create, live, list, URL), `serve.go` (the public `/f/:token`), `scan.go` (the job and schedule), `commands.go`; `store/fetchurls.go`; the module root's `notify.go`; the pages in `generation.go`/`generation.templ`. CSS for the new parts (`.gen-cols`, `.gen-col`, `.gen-fetch`, `.gen-fetchbox`, `.gen-fstate`, `.gen-cmds`, `.gen-key`, `.gen-after`, `.row.gen-hist`) is in the platform's `app.css`.

**Deviations and additions** (the contract's signatures otherwise hold):

- **`Expire(ctx, actor string)`**: the scan's `routerscript.fetch_url_expired` needs the job's actor (`job:<id>`); the contract's `Expire(ctx)` had none. When **Create fetch URL** finds a URL past its hour that the scan hasn't seen, its `fetch_url_expired` is recorded with the admin as actor, in the creating transaction.
- **`Register` uses `g.Any("/f/:token", …)`** and answers every method but `GET` with the plain `404`: with only a `GET` route Echo would answer `405` to `HEAD`/`POST`, which tells a scanner the path exists.
- Additions: `FetchURL.Live(now)`, the state constants `FetchWaiting/Used/Expired/Replaced`, `Service.URL(token)` and `MaskedURL()` (`<base>/f/••••••••`), `ScanEvery`; store `InsertFetchURL` (token `X''` with its lookup, then `SetFetchToken` with the new id's AAD), `FetchToken`, `WaitingFetchURL`, `FetchURLByLookup`, `EndFetchURL`, `UseFetchURL` (the guarded `UPDATE`: `state = 'waiting' AND expires_at > now`), `ExpiredFetchURLs`, `FetchURLs`. `Live` treats a URL used between its two reads as none.
- The fetch reads the generation and makes the file **before** the write, so a failure (`500`) leaves the URL working; the guarded `UPDATE` decides between two fetches at once (the loser gets `404`, one event). The user agent is cut to 256 characters (runes).
- **Notification**: the module renders only `routerscript.fetched` (the subject named through its own `NameSubjects`), with `notify.routerscript.fetched.body` or, without a user agent, `notify.routerscript.fetched.body_no_agent`.
- **Pages.** The Fetch URL area's `#fetch-url` box is the Reveal fragment (URL, note, both commands, **Copy both lines** `y`); masked, the fetch line shows the masked URL and every Copy button carries the real text (the token is on the page exactly three times, all in `data-copy`). Without a live URL the state line is "No fetch URL. One works once, for 1 hour.", "used at 16:41" or "expired · create a new one", with **Create fetch URL** (primary). **New fetch URL…** confirms with strength 1. **Create** answers `303` to the page's `#fetch-url`.
- **After the import** polls while a URL is live, a router awaits before its deadline, or an active router's first sync is queued (`LastResult` empty). A failed sync shows "first sync failed: <error>" and stops the polling (the router page is one click away); the registrar can't tell a first failure from a later one. The jump host is shown without `:22`. The polled answer brings `#fetch-url-state` out of band; the full page doesn't (no duplicate id). Step 1 prefers a live URL ("waiting"), then the latest used one, then "expired unused".
- **Phone**: one column with Fetch URL and After the import first; the title block (Download, Generate again) stays above them, as on every page.
- `rscriptstest`: `FakeRouters.Update(id, fn)` and `FakeKeyCommands` (the fake's routers now have key commands).
- Docs: `ui/README.md` (the generation page has no countdown: the expiry and the minutes left are rendered by the server) and `modules/router-scripts.md` follow the build, besides the contract's list.

**Checked in a real browser** (the `chromedp/headless-shell:156.0.8078.12` container over CDP, the test harness's app served on the host by a throwaway test, nothing committed): the generation page with a live URL masked; **Reveal** showed the URL and both commands in clear, **Hide** masked them again; a command's **Copy** and `y` (**Copy both lines**) put the right text on the clipboard (stubbed: the page isn't a secure context over plain http, so `navigator.clipboard` doesn't exist there); After the import polled, and once the router fetched and the fake router became active and synced it showed "fetched at … · Mikrotik/7.24.5 Fetch" and "connected at … · synced at …", the state line became "used at …" out of band, and the area lost its `hx-trigger` (the polling stopped); at 390 px one column in the order Fetch URL, After the import, Generation, Values, Fetch history, Activity, no horizontal scroll; no console error or exception.

**Not done / the user's.** The **Phase 4 exit demo** above (a spare MikroTik on RouterOS 7.24.5+, the real deployment, Telegram): `/tool fetch`'s real user agent, the zero-touch key and user lines from an imported script (open question "to verify" 5), and how a reset router gets the internet for its first fetch (open question "to verify" 9) are answered only by it. No real router has fetched or imported a generated file; the end-to-end test stops at `routerostest`. The generation page was checked in headless Chromium on a throwaway server, not on the deployed instance or a real phone.
